articles.title: The AI Infrastructure Industry Has Entered Its Coordination Crisis
articles.narrative: The AI infrastructure industry is facing a "coordination crisis" where the disparate timelines for power, cooling, electrical equipment, permitting, and construction are hindering project delivery, despite individual components being available. The author argues that the primary bottleneck is no longer a single resource but the complex orchestration required to align these various systems and stakeholders. This challenge is transforming AI infrastructure development from a traditional real estate play into a more integrated industrial systems engineering and energy infrastructure endeavor, favoring firms capable of coordinating diverse elements to deliver functional campuses on customer timelines.

articles.title: Steve Wylder On Safehold’s Plan to Fill Affordable Housing Capital Gaps
articles.narrative: Safehold, a real estate investment trust, is leveraging its ground lease strategy to address capital stack deficiencies in affordable housing developments, particularly for 4 percent Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) projects. The company's 99-year ground leases provide low-cost capital at a premium to land value, increasing permanent proceeds for developers by 10 to 20 percent and offering a lower blended cost of capital. This approach helps bridge financing gaps caused by elevated interest rates and construction costs, which have made affordable housing projects increasingly challenging to complete. Safehold has seen significant traction in Southern California, where it has closed over 25 ground leases for LIHTC developments, and is expanding its platform into markets like Texas, the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Midwest.

articles.title: Blackstone Sells Fort Lauderdale Industrial Campus for $57M
articles.narrative: Blackstone's industrial division, Link Logistics, has sold a seven-building industrial campus in Fort Lauderdale, FL, for $57 million. The 210,000-square-foot property was acquired by a joint venture between BKM Capital Partners and Kayne Anderson Real Estate. The campus, which is 97% leased, is strategically located near I-95 and the Dania Pointe retail complex, offering a strong rent roll with staggered lease expirations.

data_points.address: 2201, 2301 and 2381 Stirling Road, Fort Lauderdale, FL
data_points.notable_features: Seven small-bay buildings located less than a mile west of Interstate 95, near the Dania Pointe retail complex.
data_points.project_notes: The campus last traded for $17.5 million in 2013. The weighted average lease term is 3.9 years.

articles.title: Affinius Capital Provides $95M Construction Loan for Oregon State Student Housing
articles.narrative: Affinius Capital has provided a $94.8 million construction loan to Fields Holdings for the development of Zev Corvallis, a 13-story student housing complex near Oregon State University. The project aims to address the growing demand for student housing in Corvallis, particularly high-rise developments, driven by increasing university enrollment. The lender noted the project's potential to elevate student housing standards in the market.

data_points.address: 516 South West Fourth Street, Corvallis, OR
data_points.notable_features: 13-story high-rise student housing complex with 4,500 square feet of retail.

articles.title: Record Diesel Prices Fuel More Challenges for Retail Real Estate
articles.narrative: Record-high diesel prices, surpassing $6 per gallon in September, are significantly impacting U.S. retail real estate development by increasing transportation and construction costs. Despite strong consumer purchasing power and aggressive expansion plans from retailers, particularly in the value sector, developers face challenges due to chronically flat retail rents and compressed profit margins. This dynamic is leading to historically strained retail construction nationwide, with limited new supply available for lease, creating a competitive environment for existing quality space and favoring landlords.

articles.market_intelligence: Retail construction in Q2 2026 was historically strained nationwide. Retail vacancies are lower today than at the start of the year, and rents remain strong. Less than 30% of new retail sites are available to lease.

articles.title: MMG Real Estate Advisors Arranges Sale of 192-Unit Apartment Complex in Bryan, Texas
articles.narrative: MMG Real Estate Advisors has facilitated the sale of The Element at University Park, a 192-unit apartment complex in Bryan, Texas. Houston-based Lumen Capital sold the property to Hayden Properties. The transaction involved a regional brokerage firm, highlighting continued investment activity in Central Texas multifamily assets.

data_points.notable_features: Offers one- and two-bedroom units, sports courts (basketball, volleyball, pickleball), and a business center.

articles.title: JLL Negotiates Sale of 172,854 SF Office Building in Northwest Austin
articles.narrative: JLL has facilitated the sale of Research Park Plaza V, a 172,854-square-foot office building located in northwest Austin. The four-story property, completed in 2015, was 85 percent leased to a strong tenant mix at the time of the transaction. The seller was Cousins Properties, an Atlanta-based REIT.

articles.title: Sports Companies Sign Two Industrial Leases Totaling 150,000 SF in San Antonio
articles.narrative: Two sports-related companies, M Padel and Socceroof, have signed industrial leases totaling 150,000 square feet in San Antonio. The companies will occupy former distribution buildings on the city's northeast side, with one tenant taking 50,000 square feet and the other 150,000 square feet. The transactions reflect continued demand for large-format industrial spaces for experiential and recreational uses.

data_points.address: 6558 E. Campus Drive, San Antonio, TX
data_points.notable_features: Former distribution buildings converted for sports and recreational use.

articles.title: April Housing Underway on $21.5M Renovation of Arlington Affordable Housing Complex
articles.narrative: April Housing, the affordable housing division of Blackstone Real Estate, has commenced a $21.5 million renovation of Mayfield Park, a 240-unit complex in Arlington, TX. This renovation is part of a resyndication effort designed to extend the property's affordability status for an additional 30 years. The upgrades will encompass interior unit improvements, new mechanical systems, and enhancements to common area amenities.

data_points.notable_features: 11-building complex; renovation preserves affordability for 30 years.

articles.title: PTM Partners Obtains $125M Construction Loan for Phase II of High-Rise Project in St. Petersburg, Florida
articles.narrative: PTM Partners has secured a $125 million construction loan for the second phase of its EDGE Collective development in downtown St. Petersburg. The financing, arranged by Berkadia through an affiliate of GID, will support the construction of a 20-story residential tower with ground-floor retail. This project builds on the success of the first phase, which included a hotel and adaptive reuse components.

data_points.notable_features: 20-story residential tower with ground-floor retail space.

articles.title: Civil engineering firm signs 32,000-square-foot office lease at Triten’s Assembly Park in Plano
articles.narrative: SPIARS Engineering Inc., a civil engineering and surveying company, has signed a 32,000-square-foot office lease at Assembly Park in Plano, TX. The move will consolidate SPIARS' two existing East offices into a single location within the 26-acre mixed-use campus. The company was drawn to Assembly Park's strategic location, accessibility, design, and potential for future expansion, as well as its campus-style environment with outdoor green space, fitness amenities, and dining options.

data_points.notable_features: 26-acre walkable, mixed-use campus with creative office space, dining, luxury residences, outdoor green space, walking/biking trails, and fitness amenities.
data_points.project_notes: SPIARS Engineering Inc. is consolidating two existing offices into this single location.

articles.title: Mohr Capital closes sale of 1.05-million-square-foot industrial facility in Whiteland
articles.narrative: Mohr Capital has completed the sale of Lot 6, a 1.05-million-square-foot industrial facility located within Mohr Logistics Park in Whiteland, Indiana. The property, which was rebuilt after sustaining tornado damage in 2023, offers modern bulk warehouse space with 40-foot clear heights. The buyer and transaction terms were not disclosed, but Mohr Capital will retain ownership of the remaining portions of the logistics park.

data_points.notable_features: Modern bulk warehouse space with 40-foot clear heights, located within a 475-acre master-planned industrial development along the I-65 corridor.
data_points.project_notes: The facility was originally completed in 2022 and rebuilt on its original foundation after sustaining significant damage from an EF-3 tornado in April 2023.

articles.title: St. Louis’ S.M. Wilson & Co. names community engagement manager
BGO acquires 11-property surgery center portfolio
articles.narrative: BGO, on behalf of its U.S. Core Strategy, has acquired an 11-property portfolio of Class-A ambulatory surgery centers totaling approximately 223,000 square feet. The portfolio, which is 100% leased, was purchased from a joint venture between Flagship Healthcare Properties and AEW Capital Management. This acquisition expands BGO's healthcare real estate holdings with a geographically diversified collection of purpose-built outpatient surgical facilities across nine U.S. markets, reflecting BGO's confidence in the shift towards outpatient care delivery. Flagship Healthcare Properties will continue to provide property management services for the portfolio.

data_points.notable_features: Purpose-built Class-A ambulatory surgery centers with specialized surgical infrastructure, established affiliations with major health systems, and relationships with national ASC operators. Clinical specialties include ophthalmology, orthopedics, gastroenterology, ENT, podiatry, plastic and reconstructive surgery, pain management, urology, and endoscopy.

articles.title: Mid-America brokers sale of 240,345-square-foot community center in Lombard
articles.narrative: Mid-America Real Estate Corporation's Investment Sales Group facilitated the sale of High Point Centre, a 240,345-square-foot community center in Lombard, Illinois. The property, located in the affluent western DuPage County Chicago suburbs, was acquired by a private investment group from a publicly traded REIT. The center offers significant value-add potential, currently operating at 68% occupancy with a diverse tenant mix.

data_points.notable_features: Community center with value-add upside, located along heavily trafficked Roosevelt Road.

articles.title: Yamaha Divests U.S. Headquarters in Sale-Leaseback
articles.narrative: Yamaha Motor Corporation, U.S.A. has completed a sale-leaseback transaction for its U.S. headquarters campus in Cypress, CA. The Walt Disney Co. acquired the 25-acre, 278,964-square-foot property for $115 million, intending to utilize it for back-office operations. Yamaha will continue to occupy the campus through December 2028 as it prepares for a planned relocation to Kennesaw, GA. The transaction highlights the strong demand for high-caliber assets in the local market.

data_points.notable_features: Infill industrial-zoned property includes one industrial, one flex, and one office building.
data_points.project_notes: Yamaha will lease back the property through December 31, 2028, as part of a planned relocation to Kennesaw, GA. The property has served as Yamaha's U.S. headquarters since 1979.

articles.title: Houston Industrial Market Stays Strong
articles.narrative: Houston's industrial market experienced a significant surge in the third quarter of 2026, marking its strongest leasing activity in over four years. This acceleration was driven by a notable increase in large transactions, with nineteen leases exceeding 250,000 square feet signed during the quarter. The market also saw robust net absorption, indicating strong demand for industrial space.

articles.title: Trammell Crow-Led JV Sells Houston Warehouse for $26.8M
articles.narrative: A joint venture led by Trammell Crow Company and Daiwa House Texas Inc. has sold Building 3 of the Blue Ridge Commerce Center in Houston, Texas, to Applied Optoelectronics for $26.8 million. The 153,928-square-foot warehouse was fully leased by the buyer in February 2026, prior to the sale. This transaction marks the fourth building sold to an owner-occupier within the first phase of the commerce center, highlighting strong demand for industrial properties in the area.

data_points.property_name: Building 3 at Blue Ridge Commerce Center
data_points.address: 16851 Blue Ridge Commerce Dr, Houston, TX
data_points.project_notes: Building 3 was delivered in Fall 2025 as part of Phase I, which included five warehouse buildings totaling 1.35 million square feet. The buyer had leased 100% of the building in February 2026.

articles.title: Agora Starting Last Phase of $375M N. Las Vegas Development
articles.narrative: Agora Realty has commenced construction on the third and final phase of Hylo Park, a 73-acre master-planned mixed-use community in North Las Vegas. This $375 million, 25-acre phase will create a youth sports and sports tourism-focused entertainment district, featuring a multi-sport indoor field house, an existing arena, a sports academy, retail, restaurants, and a 177-key Hilton Embassy Suites. The project is slated for completion in late 2027.

data_points.notable_features: Professional-level, mixed-use youth sports-and sports tourism-focused walkable entertainment district with complementary amenities.
data_points.project_notes: This is the third and final phase of a 73-acre master-planned community. Phase two, Hylo Park South, a 90,750-square-foot grocery-anchored retail center, was completed in July 2026. Phase one involved the sale of 36.5 acres to Lennar Corp. for residential development in late 2024.

articles.title: Arizona Biltmore Owners Buy Wrigley Mansion
articles.narrative: A joint venture led by Henderson Park, in partnership with Western & Southern Financial Group, Hamilton Lane, South Street Partners, and Pyramid Global Hospitality, has acquired the historic Wrigley Mansion in Phoenix, AZ, for $17 million. The property was sold by the Hormel family, who had owned it for 34 years. This acquisition brings the Wrigley Mansion under the same ownership as the nearby Arizona Biltmore, which the Henderson Park-led venture purchased in 2024.

data_points.notable_features: Perched atop a 100-foot knoll, offering sweeping 360-degree views of the Valley.
data_points.project_notes: Commissioned by William Wrigley Jr. as a 50th wedding anniversary gift for his wife, Ada.

articles.title: Ireland On Course For €3B Of Real Estate Investment In 2026
articles.narrative: Ireland's real estate market is projected to attract €3 billion in investment by the end of 2026, driven by a significant increase in deal activity during the third quarter. This forecast suggests a robust recovery and sustained investor confidence in the Irish property sector.

articles.title: South Fulton Mayor Embraces Data Centers After End Of Moratorium
articles.narrative: The mayor of South Fulton, GA, has publicly endorsed data center development, emphasizing their economic benefits and necessity for the city's growth. This stance comes after the expiration of a moratorium on new data center projects in the area, signaling a shift towards embracing the industry despite broader national concerns.

articles.title: Life Insurers Writing Riskier Loans To CRE, Setting Off Alarm Bells
articles.narrative: Life insurance companies significantly increased their leverage on commercial real estate loans during the first half of the year, outpacing all other investor types. This trend is raising concerns among market observers regarding potential risks in the CRE lending landscape.

articles.title: Lawmakers Are Canceling Data Center Tax Breaks. Developers Are Learning To Adapt
articles.narrative: State and local governments are increasingly rescinding tax breaks for data center developments due to rising public opposition. This trend is forcing developers to adjust their strategies for new projects.
